feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
entry.summary:
EnvHarness and EnvRigger introduce a programmable layer and automated synthesis system that dynamically wraps static LLM agent environments to target policy weaknesses without altering underlying logic or verifiers.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to manually build domain-specific environment pipelines, allowing existing agent environments to automatically adapt and scale training to specific policy weaknesses.

entry.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
entry.summary:
FACET is a framework that synthesizes complex terminal agent tasks by preserving original source intent and using a shared, repaired container state to ensure consistency across instructions, solutions, and verifiers.

Why it matters: It enables the scalable, data-efficient synthesis of complex, validated terminal tasks needed to train and evaluate command-line agents reliably.

entry.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
entry.summary:
4DAnyone reconstructs 4D humans from monocular video by using 4D Gaussian Splatting combined with a video diffusion model that scales to tens of consistent novel views.

Why it matters: It overcomes context-length limits in video diffusion models, enabling high-fidelity 4D human reconstruction and novel-view rendering from casual, uncalibrated single-camera videos.

entry.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
entry.summary:
WithEveryone is a unified framework that scales group image generation up to ten reference identities by injecting identity-addressed tokens and applying Layout-Grounded ID Loss with ID Representation Forcing.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, multi-person image generation for large groups without suffering from duplicate faces, missed identities, or reference copy-paste artifacts.

entry.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
entry.summary:
MemTrapBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate memory-induced cognitive traps in LLMs, revealing that faithfully retrieved memories can degrade model reasoning and performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard long-term LLM memory retrieval can actively impair reasoning and task performance, highlighting the need for defensive inference strategies like AdaptiveMem.

entry.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
entry.summary:
SWE-bench Science is a new repository-level benchmark containing 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.

Why it matters: It establishes a concrete evaluation benchmark exposing how current AI coding agents fail when modifying complex scientific codebases where software errors risk invalidating scientific results.

entry.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents
entry.summary:
FM-Bench evaluates LLM agents over a 20-year horizon using 26 tools and up to 400 decision stops to manage a football club against deterministic engines and competing agents in a shared Arena without human judges.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that long-horizon agent performance depends on strategic operational behaviors rather than compute scale, while highlighting critical failure modes in LLM memory management and market inference.

entry.title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models
entry.summary:
ForgeWM is a four-stage progressive training framework that converts bidirectional action-conditioned video generators into efficient 1-, 2-, and 4-step causal world models for game control.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, low-latency interactive video generation driven by fast-paced user controls without sacrificing visual quality or control alignment.

entry.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution
entry.summary:
SkillForge is a self-distillation framework that proactively acquires project-specific knowledge by synthesizing and solving synthetic issues generated from test-covered repository code.

Why it matters: Proactively extracting and grounding codebase knowledge before encountering real issues enables LLM agents to resolve repository-specific bugs more accurately and efficiently.

entry.title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation
entry.summary:
VA-Judger is a chain-of-thought omni-reward model that uses dimension-wise reinforcement learning on human preference data to improve joint video-audio generation quality.

Why it matters: It provides a human-aligned reward signal for post-training joint video-audio models, preventing reward hacking and improving overall semantic and temporal coherence.

entry.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
entry.summary:
Repo0 is a continuous structural evolution framework for zero-to-all code generation that constructs software projects from natural-language requirements using a Dual-Directed-Acyclic-Graph (Dual-DAG) architectural state.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to generate complete, modular software repositories from scratch without needing a predefined architecture.

entry.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
entry.summary:
FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention into a production-ready engine using mean error correction, optimized FP8 GPU kernels, and native paged KV cache integration.

Why it matters: It transforms theoretical block-sparse prefill optimizations into a deployable backend that drastically speeds up 128K long-context LLM serving in production frameworks.

entry.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
entry.summary:
The IAR framework improves retrieval-free document knowledge internalization by staging post-training into structured document knowledge injection, answer-only QA alignment, and general capability recovery via model merging.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to accurately answer domain-specific questions without retrieval augmentation while preserving general instruction-following and reasoning abilities.

entry.title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
SkillGate resolves selector credit starvation in long-horizon agents by splitting credit into distinct outcome-reward channels for execution and local advantage channels for skill selection.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon agents to accurately select required skills from large libraries without being degraded by noisy sequence-level reinforcement learning rewards.

entry.title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery
entry.summary:
The Find, Attempt, and Recommend (FAR) framework automates problem discovery and filtering from literature, reducing human bottlenecks in AI-assisted mathematical research.

Why it matters: It optimizes scarce expert review time and model reasoning resources by automating the search and pre-filtering of mathematical open problems.

entry.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
AI4AI-Bench introduces 10 frozen research repositories to evaluate LLM agents on rewriting training algorithms for recursive self-improvement, where top systems close less than a fifth of the gap to task optima.

Why it matters: The benchmark isolates an agent's capability to improve core learning algorithms rather than just tuning hyperparameters, offering an empirical measure of progress toward recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation
entry.summary:
A novel method enables reasoning language models to adaptively select their reasoning depth via a initial token choice, reducing inference token usage while maintaining accuracy.

Why it matters: This approach significantly lowers test-time compute costs and latency by dynamically scaling reasoning effort based on problem difficulty without needing an external routing model.

entry.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
entry.summary:
A two-step hyperparameter transfer framework uses Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) and scaling laws to accurately predict optimal learning rates for large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models across both model widths and token counts.

Why it matters: It enables accurate tuning of optimal learning rates for massive MoE models using small proxy models, drastically reducing the computational cost of hyperparameter sweeps.

entry.title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Large Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
EchoCoT is a new multi-step attack framework that extracts near-verbatim hidden chain-of-thought traces from black-box large reasoning models via API tool-call interactions.

Why it matters: It establishes hidden chain-of-thought extraction as a practical security and intellectual property risk for proprietary black-box reasoning models.

entry.title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
entry.summary:
In-context secrets implicitly leak into benign language model outputs, enabling an adaptive black-box attack to reconstruct sensitive data even when direct extraction is refused.

Why it matters: AI agents handling sensitive user data risk exposing confidential context through routine, benign responses even when explicit safety guardrails prevent direct extraction.

entry.title: Learning how to Forget: Fine-tuning for Long-Context Sparse Attention
entry.summary:
A new fine-tuning method allows transformer models to co-adapt with any sparse attention KV cache policy using moderate hardware, outperforming models trained with exact attention.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective fine-tuning and improved long-context inference performance without requiring massive GPU clusters for sequence parallelism.

entry.title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment
entry.summary:
LoRA-GA$^2$ improves low-rank adaptation by using multi-step gradient information from pretrained weights alongside spectrum-aware rank allocation and optimal initialization.

Why it matters: It narrows the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning without increasing memory overhead.

entry.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
entry.summary:
A study auditing LLM agent step-level credit signals against causal ground-truth from executed replays in ALFWorld shows that common credit rules perform no better than chance and primarily echo policy fluency rather than causal step contribution.

Why it matters: Reinforcement learning and fine-tuning methods for LLM agents currently rely on step-level credit signals that fail to reflect actual causal impact, meaning training efficiency is dictated by sample volume rather than true credit assignment.

entry.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
entry.summary:
FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention for production LLM serving by adding a mean correction term for low FP8/BF16 approximation error and optimizing memory access for engines like SGLang.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between theoretical sparse attention research and production LLM serving by drastically reducing long-context prefill latency in modern inference frameworks.

entry.title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification
entry.summary:
TUP is a Best-of-N distillation method that truncates low-ranked candidate completions from the target support and reweights the retained upper tail using a tunable sharpness parameter.

Why it matters: It enables efficient offline policy distillation from Best-of-N sampling without relying on brittle top-rank reward model distinctions or retaining low-quality completions in the target support.

entry.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
entry.summary:
A contrastive study analyzes LLM agent skills to reveal they primarily act as procedural execution anchors rather than knowledge injectors, while identifying retrieval bottlenecks and failure modes.

Why it matters: Understanding that skills act as procedural anchors rather than fact injectors guides the design of better retrieval mechanisms and more robust self-evolving LLM agents.

entry.title: Zetta ζ: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
entry.summary:
Zetta is a closed-loop embodied harness that evolves code-based runtime critics and recovery skills online over three timescale-separated loops while keeping the base policy frozen.

Why it matters: It establishes an efficient scaling path for reliable physical intelligence by enabling real-time execution governance and self-evolving recovery skills without expensive policy retraining.

entry.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL
entry.summary:
Co-RL enables unsupervised reasoning in LLMs and VLMs through multi-agent reinforcement learning using peer-derived rewards from a diverse model cohort.

Why it matters: It eliminates the reliance on costly, hard-to-scale ground-truth reward annotations for training advanced reasoning models across text and multimodal domains.

entry.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation
entry.summary:
SemComp-Bench introduces an outcome-oriented benchmark and VLM-based evaluation protocol for video generation, focusing on semantic task completion and grounding rather than intermediate steps or appearance consistency.

Why it matters: It shifts video generation evaluation from strict appearance consistency and full sequence tracking toward functional, goal-oriented task completion.

entry.title: SemaPLC: A Project-Grounded, Verification-Gated Agent Harness for PLC Code Generation
entry.summary:
SemaPLC is an open-source, verification-gated agent harness for PLC code generation that enforces task completion using external compilation, specification, and live runtime trace execution checks.

Why it matters: It establishes live runtime execution and trace comparison, rather than static analysis, as the necessary standard for validating generated industrial control logic.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
entry.summary:
SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as an Environment Designer generating executable OpenAI Gym-style environments and a Reasoning Agent that learns to solve them.

Why it matters: Making the environment generator a learnable component solves the goal-stagnation problem in RL, enabling open-ended self-improvement for autonomous language agents.

entry.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
entry.summary:
EditBridge enables faithful ultra-high-resolution (up to 4K) image editing by framing refinement as structured data-to-data translation conditioned on the original high-resolution source using block-wise sparse attention.

Why it matters: It eliminates the quadratic memory constraints of high-resolution diffusion models, enabling fast, artifact-free 4K image editing in professional workflows.

entry.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization
entry.summary:
DiSCO is a zero-shot, black-box defense that uses distribution-guided suffix expansion and contrastive scoring to optimize prompts, preventing NSFW content generation without modifying model weights.

Why it matters: It provides an architecture-agnostic, zero-shot safety defense that can be deployed directly in front of proprietary, black-box text-to-image models without altering their underlying code or weights.

entry.title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
LEGO-RL bridges long-running native coding-agent harnesses with policy-gradient training using in-process LLM proxying and isolated sandbox orchestration without modifying internal harness control flows.

Why it matters: It enables reliable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM coding agents directly within off-the-shelf agent execution harnesses without corrupting training signals.

entry.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification
entry.summary:
A data-free, white-box lineage verification method uses centered residual signatures from weight matrices to accurately identify open-weight language model ancestry across multiple model families.

Why it matters: It enables passive, fast, and reliable auditability of open-weight LLMs to verify model provenance and detect unauthorized re-skinning or laundering without requiring dataset access.

entry.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis
entry.summary:
Researchers trained C3LM using Top-K prompting on a 45.6M reaction dataset and fine-tuned it with ChemCensor-based and novelty rewards for retrosynthesis.

Why it matters: Plausibility-aware Top-K training enables LLMs to generate more diverse and valid reaction pathways, advancing computer-aided synthesis planning.

entry.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding
entry.summary:
MoE-ViE applies fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, custom inference kernels, and frame-level distillation to scale CLIP-style vision encoders efficiently for image and video understanding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that MoE vision encoders can achieve state-of-the-art vision-language multimodal performance while significantly reducing compute costs and inference latency compared to dense architectures.

entry.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated looped language models on compositional tool calling, finding that recurrent computation at inference time significantly improves multi-step tool coordination, state maintenance, and dependency resolution.

Why it matters: Looped architectures allow agentic AI systems to execute complex multi-step tool workflows more reliably by dynamically allocating compute during inference without increasing parameter count.

entry.title: Decision-Metric Alignment in Latent World Models: Diagnostics and Action-Conditioned Objectives for MPC Planning
entry.summary:
This paper introduces diagnostics and an action-conditioned objective, DA-LeWM, to fix decision-metric misalignment where latent distance fails to correctly rank action sequences in MPC planning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that strong latent decoding performance is insufficient for planning, proving that explicitly optimizing latent geometry for decision alignment significantly improves online MPC success.

entry.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
entry.summary:
SoftVTBench introduces a dataset of 4,000 expert visuo-tactile demonstrations with FEM ground-truth and a benchmark evaluating deformable-object manipulation via a novel Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR).

Why it matters: It establishes that standard task-completion metrics overlook physical damage during manipulation, providing a standardized framework to develop safer multimodal policies.

entry.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters
entry.summary:
Harness Continual Learning (HCL) introduces a framework for evolving a frozen foundation model's external harness—including prompts, memories, tools, and routers—while mitigating harness-level catastrophic forgetting.

Why it matters: HCL enables persistent agent improvement and failure recovery through external prompt and memory updates without expensive model fine-tuning or parameter degradation.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Why Exploitation, Not Exploration, Is the Bottleneck
entry.summary:
A compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains reveals that test-time scaling fails due to poor candidate exploitation rather than insufficient exploration.

Why it matters: Increasing inference compute via current test-time scaling methods yields diminishing returns in open-ended domains unless reward models and candidate selection mechanisms are substantially improved.

entry.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
EvoResearcher is a training-free inference protocol that implements cost-bounded self-reflection and early stopping on a frozen LLM backbone without gradient updates.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to self-verify and optimize compute budgets at inference time without requiring costly reinforcement learning pipelines like GRPO.

entry.title: Learned, Then Lost: A Measured Single-Example Counterfactual in Pre-training
entry.summary:
Researchers measured the exact counterfactual impact of a single 194-token training injection across 32 124M-parameter GPT-2 models, finding the memory rapidly decays and leaves no detectable final trace on loss barriers or CKA.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that single-example pre-training memory rapidly decays without altering final loss basins provides empirical grounding for counterfactual data attribution and privacy limits in large language models.

entry.title: Gradient Mirage: Trainable yet Label-Unidentifiable Gradients in Large Language Model Split Learning
entry.summary:
Gradient Mirage defends LLM split learning against gradient matching attacks by disrupting gradient-objective consistency while preserving model utility.

Why it matters: It enables secure split learning of large language models by preventing malicious servers from recovering private training labels from shared interface gradients.

entry.title: WhiteMatter: All-to-All Cross-Layer Connections via KV Mixing
entry.summary:
WhiteMatter introduces all-to-all cross-layer connections that route and mix a token's L layer states into k KV-cache channels for subsequent consumer layers to attend to.

Why it matters: It improves Transformer parameter efficiency and performance while significantly reducing KV-cache memory overhead during decoding.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
entry.summary:
SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as both an Environment Designer generating executable code environments and a Reasoning Agent learning to solve them.

Why it matters: By making environment synthesis learnable and adaptive rather than static, SPADE enables continuous open-ended self-improvement for language models across complex reasoning and tool-use tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (GC-OPD) resolves teacher-verifier misalignment in long-context reasoning by combining group-normalized trajectory residuals with token-level Relative-Advantage-Based Credit Assignment (RACA).

Why it matters: It enables long-context language models to retain dense token-level training guidance from teacher models while ensuring alignment with global, response-level task verifiers.

entry.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
entry.summary:
Verifiable Latent Alignments (VLA) is a framework that monitors and mitigates covert language-model multi-agent communication in continuous hidden states using an activation-aware, neutral-only three-layer monitor and matched counterfactual steering.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that covert, non-transcript multi-agent collusion via continuous hidden states can be effectively detected and steered back to neutral behavior without prior training on attack patterns.

entry.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Open-MOPD diagnoses capability integration failures in multi-teacher on-policy distillation and introduces three budget-rebalancing mechanisms, improving headroom recovery from 35.6% to 83.4% on SmolLM3-3B-Base.

Why it matters: It enables the effective consolidation of multiple domain-specialized RL expert models into a single generalist student without suffering severe cross-domain performance degradation.

entry.title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
entry.summary:
StateM is an agent-native runtime that uses harness scaling—durable states, phase-local context, and versioned runbooks—to reach 95.3% raw accuracy on Terminal-Bench 2.1 without updating model weights.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that runtime harness engineering can outperform model-scaling approaches for long-horizon agent tasks while drastically reducing API compute costs.

entry.title: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
SA-MRPO replaces fixed scalarized rewards in multi-objective RL with independent per-objective standardization and dynamic saturation-based advantage reweighting.

Why it matters: It dynamically redirects model capacity toward unfulfilled objectives during post-training without requiring manual tuning of multi-reward weights or risking performance degradation on mastered tasks.

entry.title: Large Discovery Models: Empirically-grounded Model-Based Open-Ended Search
entry.summary:
The Large Discovery Model couples generative models with a Bayesian non-parametric reward surrogate and dynamic memory to enable uncertainty-aware, empirically grounded search across open-ended hypothesis spaces.

Why it matters: Combining generative priors with calibrated statistical surrogates allows AI systems to discover optimized molecules, proteins, and neural architectures far more reliably than LLM self-reflection alone.

entry.title: MOSS-VL Technical Report
entry.summary:
MOSS-VL is an 11.3B open vision-language model family co-designed for real-time interaction using gated cross-attention to process incoming visual frames while generating text.

Why it matters: It enables open-source vision-language models to handle real-time proactive interaction and large visual contexts with significantly lower first-token latency.

entry.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence
entry.summary:
ASI-Bench is a new benchmark featuring 60 project-level research tasks across 11 scientific domains to evaluate AI systems' autonomous exploration and execution capabilities as human methodological guidance is progressively removed.

Why it matters: The dramatic performance drop under unguided conditions reveals that state-of-the-art AI agents remain heavily reliant on human guidance and are currently unable to autonomously execute end-to-end scientific research.

entry.title: FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution
entry.summary:
FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving system that dynamically adapts model layout, expert residency, and CPU-GPU execution to local, heterogeneous hardware resources.

Why it matters: It enables consumer-grade edge hardware and single workstations to locally serve frontier-scale MoE models that previously required datacenter infrastructure.

entry.title: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements
entry.summary:
Agentic ESOpt is a full-parameter agentic fine-tuning framework using Evolution Strategies to train long-horizon LLM agents with minimal inference-level GPU memory requirements.

Why it matters: It enables full-parameter fine-tuning of large LLM agents on long-horizon tasks using low-memory, inference-only hardware without the stability and compute overhead of multi-turn RL.

entry.title: How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch: End-to-End Diagnostic Evaluation on 100 Real-World Frontier Research Tasks
entry.summary:
AutoResearchEval introduces 100 full-lifecycle frontier science tasks to diagnose AI agent failures, establishing a 45-pattern taxonomy based on 800 evaluated trajectories.

Why it matters: Understanding systematically how autonomous research agents fail reveals that model-level metacognitive deficits, rather than scaffolding issues, currently limit end-to-end scientific discovery.

entry.title: Advancing Open and Reproducible Relational Learning: RelArena-α, TabPFN-Rel and RPI
entry.summary:
Prior Labs released an open-source alpha suite for relational learning comprising the RelArena-α benchmark framework, the TabPFN-Rel model harness, and the model-agnostic Relational Predictive Interface (RPI).

Why it matters: It establishes standardized benchmarking for relational ML while offering tools to apply tabular models like TabPFN directly to relational databases.

entry.title: Embodied-Navigator: Point, Think, Memorize, and Align for Efficient Navigation
entry.summary:
TAMP-Nav is a unified embodied navigation framework that combines a 2D pixel-to-3D action formulation, dynamic selective reasoning with compressed memory, and GRPO-based two-level alignment.

Why it matters: It improves VLM deployment efficiency in robotics by aligning action spaces with 2D pre-training priors and reducing sample complexity.

entry.title: GRNEdit: Efficient General Video Editing from a New Binary-Evidence Perspective in Generative Refinement Networks
entry.summary:
GRNEdit is a lightweight two-stage video editing framework that models source video information as binary-evidence signals and refines target-bit decisions using a source-preserving identity pathway.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lightweight binary-evidence conditioning can outperform or match much larger 14B parameter video editing models while significantly reducing computational overhead.

entry.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL
entry.summary:
Agent Lightning v1.0 is a 3,500-line framework for harnessed agentic RL, enabling post-training of arbitrary agent harnesses through an LLM proxy.

Why it matters: It allows developers to post-train language models directly within their existing production agent harnesses using minimal compute and data.

entry.title: CoinVE-200K: A Large-Scale High-Quality Dataset for Compositional Instruction-Guided Video Editing
entry.summary:
CoinVE-200K is a large-scale video editing dataset offering 1080p video pairs with up to 201 frames and 2 to 5 compositional editing operations per sample, paired with a benchmark and the 22B CoinVE-Edit model.

Why it matters: It provides the dataset, benchmark, and architectural framework necessary to advance video editing models from single-intent tasks to complex, multi-operation compositional edits.

entry.title: TRACE-Bench: Decomposing and Diagnosing Multi-Reference Image Generation
entry.summary:
TRACE-Bench introduces a capability-oriented framework for multi-reference image generation, decomposing complex tasks into four atomic operators across 1,600 evaluation cases to precisely locate model failure modes.

Why it matters: By shifting from holistic task scores to granular, operator-level diagnostics, TRACE-Bench reveals that multi-reference generation failures stem from attribute binding and disentanglement rather than overall composition.

entry.title: Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a unified controlled harness evaluation across 26 metrics to analyze how different memory substrates perform across various LLM backbones, history lengths, and task regimes.

Why it matters: The findings show that memory architecture must be dynamically routed based on task type and history length rather than relying on a single static substrate.

entry.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing
entry.summary:
Researchers developed J64, a 64-axis internal semantic readout for MoE reasoning models, and its routing-based proxy R64, enabling non-intrusive model monitoring, trace-free test-time intervention, and targeted router editing.

Why it matters: Native MoE routing statistics can act as a zero-overhead proxy for latent reasoning states, allowing real-time decoding interventions and targeted model edits without relying on generated token traces.

entry.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference
entry.summary:
MoNe is a lightweight modular neural memory that attaches to frozen Transformers, providing O(N) preprocessing and O(1) query costs for long-context inference without context re-reading or backbone retraining.

Why it matters: MoNe enables large language models to process extreme context lengths with constant-time query overhead and fixed peak GPU memory usage without fine-tuning the base model.

entry.title: Recirculation
entry.summary:
Recirculation is an inference-time architectural enhancement that introduces recurrence into feedforward transformers to track belief states without adding generation latency.

Why it matters: It allows foundation models to significantly improve generation and reasoning performance at inference time without requiring computationally expensive model retraining or adding token generation latency.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF
entry.summary:
Reinforcement learning using a two-player adversarial debate game reduces reward hacking when an LLM policy is overseen by a weaker AI judge compared to standard RLAIF.

Why it matters: Debate training provides a viable scalable oversight mechanism to prevent policy models from exploiting weaker AI evaluators as model capabilities advance.

entry.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement
entry.summary:
Chain-of-Experience (CoE) enables LLMs to continuously improve at test time by accumulating iterative experiential traces from self-feedback and environmental signals.

Why it matters: CoE provides a token-efficient framework for continuous test-time model optimization without requiring retraining or manual fine-tuning.

entry.title: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that stateful defenses fail against LLM decomposition attacks executed across unlinkable identities, proving theoretical limits and achieving up to 100% attack success within two attempts across 10 tested defense policies.

Why it matters: Stateful monitors alone cannot stop multi-identity decomposition attacks, necessitating structural mitigations like identity linkage, costs for fresh accounts, or restricted answer usage.

entry.title: PTXBench: Benchmark and Adapt LLMs for GPU Kernel Optimization with Architecture-specific PTX
entry.summary:
PTXBench evaluates and adapts LLMs for architecture-specific PTX GPU kernel optimization across GEMM and attention workloads on H100 and B200 GPUs.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized benchmark to measure and improve how well LLMs write hardware-specific assembly instructions to optimize deep learning kernels for new GPU architectures.

entry.title: What Tokens are Learned when Tokenization is Optimized Jointly with Language Modeling?
entry.summary:
Jointly optimizing tokenization with language modeling alters token structures, with SSLMs learning morphologically aligned tokens and H-Nets favoring byte-level efficiency over traditional subword vocabularies.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that tokenizer-free, jointly optimized approaches effectively automate vocabulary creation by prioritizing contextual and computational efficiency over fixed morphological rules.

entry.title: Q-Interference: Memory-Efficient Phase-Aware Quantum-Inspired Attention
entry.summary:
Q-Interference introduces a memory-efficient, phase-aware quantum-inspired attention mechanism for GPT models using an exact trigonometric factorization.

Why it matters: It enables richer, phase-aware feature interactions in Transformer attention mechanisms without increasing memory overhead or breaking compatibility with standard GPT pipelines.

entry.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
entry.summary:
A comprehensive re-evaluation reveals that memory-based self-improving agents suffer from extreme fragility due to amplified variance, sensitivity to task ordering, and task or environment underspecification.

Why it matters: Evaluating self-improving agents requires multi-run protocols and randomized task orders to prevent false conclusions drawn from unstated curricula and environment noise.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation (S^2VOPD) creates an informative teacher-student asymmetry without privileged labels or stronger models by distilling an unaugmented visual distribution into a strongly augmented student view.

Why it matters: It enables state-of-the-art visual reasoning capabilities in smaller vision-language models without requiring ground-truth annotations, human reward signals, or larger teacher models.

entry.title: VibeWorlding: Can Multimodal Agents Construct 3D Open Worlds End-to-End?
entry.summary:
VibeWorlding introduces a framework, benchmark, sandbox environment, and multimodal RL-trained models to evaluate and improve end-to-end 3D open world construction by multimodal agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted reinforcement learning post-training can allow open-source MLLMs to outperform leading proprietary models in complex 3D tool use and spatial world generation.

entry.title: HarnessEval-W: Agentifying the Evaluation of Visual Worlds
entry.summary:
HarnessEval-W is an agentified evaluation pipeline for visual world models that replaces scalar metrics with a transparent, verifiable evidence tree generated by specialized sub-agents.

Why it matters: It replaces opaque, brute-force scalar metrics with interpretable and verifiable reasoning chains to accurately assess physics and causality in world model rollouts.

entry.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness
entry.summary:
ClawGym II introduces a unified black-box RL framework using sandbox execution infrastructure and proxy-intercepted trajectory prefix trees to train agents like Qwen3-30A3B through complex, heterogeneous harnesses.

Why it matters: It enables stable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM agents operating within complex, black-box execution harnesses on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
SimpleOPD enables tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation from long-context teacher models to short-context students using shared text-space token alignment and constrained reference KL loss.

Why it matters: It allows smaller, short-context open-weights models to efficiently acquire advanced long-form reasoning capabilities from specialized teachers without requiring identical tokenizers.

entry.title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
entry.summary:
UI-Mate is an open-weight 27B GUI foundation agent trained with an environment-grounded stack and in-context demonstration learning, setting new open-weight state-of-the-art performance on OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining in-context multimodal demonstrations with online RL substantially improves the execution reliability of open-weight models during long-horizon desktop automation tasks.

entry.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data
entry.summary:
Mimir v1 is an open 1-billion-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model trained from scratch using only permissible post-training data across 161 datasets.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive frontier performance in smaller language models can be achieved using strictly ethically sourced and permissible datasets.

entry.title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the concept of agentic transactions, framing LLM agent execution around an ACID-compliant framework featuring four semantic guarantees to improve reliability in dynamic workflows.

Why it matters: Adapting database transactional guarantees to agent architectures provides a principled mechanism for reliable, safe, and durable long-horizon task execution.

entry.title: GenRouter: Unified Workflow Routing for Agentic Image Generation
entry.summary:
GenRouter is the first unified workflow routing framework for agentic image generation, dynamically routing prompts to optimal workflow topologies to improve visual alignment while cutting compute costs by over 95%.

Why it matters: It prevents compute-mismatch in agentic image generation by dynamically matching prompt complexity to the necessary workflow, drastically reducing operational latency and cost.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
Researchers established a latent-to-pixel training strategy that overcomes slow pixel-space pre-training, enabling pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models to match or exceed latent-space performance while achieving up to 4.75x inference speedups.

Why it matters: This recipe eliminates the efficiency trade-off of pixel-space diffusion models, delivering significantly faster end-to-end image generation without compromising output quality.

entry.title: MegaParts: Scaling Part-Aware 3D Object Generation to 300 Parts via Token-Efficient Autoregressive Modeling
entry.summary:
MegaParts is an autoregressive 3D generation framework using a token-efficient vector-quantized shape tokenizer to scale part-aware generation up to 300 parts and 256k-token sequence lengths.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that token-efficient autoregressive modeling can replace diffusion models for high-fidelity 3D object generation requiring complex, fine-grained part assemblies.

entry.title: Understanding Cognition-Induced Risks in Agentic AI Systems
entry.summary:
A new framework categorizes cognition-induced risks in LLM-powered agentic AI systems across physical, social, and self-referential levels to analyze threats to human agency, autonomy, and control.

Why it matters: Systematically categorizing how expanding AI cognitive capabilities threaten human control provides a structured foundation for designing actionable safety guardrails in autonomous agentic systems.

entry.title: R^3-Bench: LLMs Struggle with Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared Budgets
entry.summary:
R^3-Bench introduces a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on resource-rational reasoning under shared computational budgets across math, programming, and abstract reasoning in tool-free and agentic environments.

Why it matters: Current LLMs suffer from a gap between their baseline problem-solving competence and their ability to dynamically allocate compute under global budget constraints.

entry.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs
entry.summary:
Ventor-QTest is a black-box audit tool that evaluates vendor-hosted LLM API fidelity using repeated requests and long-sequence probes without requiring logprob access.

Why it matters: It enables model consumers to audit third-party API quality and detect silent performance degradation in long-horizon agentic workflows without relying on vendor-provided log probabilities.

entry.title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding
entry.summary:
VideoGAIA is a new benchmark featuring 271 model-human co-designed tasks that evaluates multimodal models on multi-turn, tool-augmented agentic video understanding.

Why it matters: It establishes a harder, tool-use-focused benchmark to drive the evolution of multimodal LLMs from static video question answering to dynamic, agentic interaction.

entry.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers naturally-occurring LLM behaviors and generates explanations evaluated through counterfactual prompt edits.

Why it matters: CHIVE provides an automated framework to rigorously evaluate interpretability techniques and produce training data that improves counterfactual reasoning about LLM behavior.

entry.title: Le Critique: Privileged Value Functions for LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Le Critique introduces Privileged Value Functions (PVF) and the TETHER baseline to enhance token-level credit assignment and performance in LLM reinforcement learning over standard value functions and GRPO.

Why it matters: The approach makes learned value functions more practical and performant for LLM training, offering fine-grained token-level credit assignment without relying on large rollout groups.

entry.title: Does the LM Head Create a Harmful Gradient Bottleneck? A Causal Test
entry.summary:
A backward-only intervention study isolates LM-head gradient rank reduction, showing that while gradient compression exists, it is far less harmful than forward-pass factorized projections and does not constitute a primary optimization bottleneck.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that geometric compression in the LM head does not severely bottleneck optimization, indicating that architectural modifications targeting gradient rank projection yield minimal optimization benefits.

entry.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals
entry.summary:
HalluTracer is a white-box detection framework that aggregates weakly correlated truthfulness signals across all network layers during the forward pass using depth averaging to reduce noise.

Why it matters: By capturing truthfulness signals distributed across the entire model depth rather than relying on single-layer probes, developers can build more reliable hallucination detectors for high-stakes LLM deployments.

entry.title: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation: Interpolating Between On-Policy Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Step-Level On-Policy Distillation (SOPD) provides step-level teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories to interpolate between the long-horizon corrections of SFT and the state-alignment advantages of OPD.

Why it matters: SOPD provides a superior distillation framework for reasoning and agent tasks by combining long-horizon path corrections with on-policy state alignment.

entry.title: Prior Audit-Repair Context Shifts LLM Verifier Thresholds Toward Leniency
entry.summary:
Including a completed audit-repair episode in an LLM verifier's context systematically shifts its decision threshold toward leniency, reducing false alarm rates on subsequent tasks by 2.8 to 11.5 percentage points.

Why it matters: Wiring LLM checkers and fixers sequentially alters the checker's baseline severity threshold, meaning verifier accuracy and strictness depend heavily on prior in-context interaction history.

entry.title: From Sequence to Structure: Relational Uncertainty Propagation for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
RUPA is a trajectory-level uncertainty quantification framework for LLM agents that models execution histories as directed dependency graphs to propagate risk across long-range reasoning steps, tool interactions, and environment feedback.

Why it matters: By accounting for long-range dependency chains rather than isolated step probabilities, RUPA enables earlier detection of agent failures and improves execution reliability in complex, long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a state integrity failure where language agents retaining KV-cache state attend to logically aborted transcript branches, breaking rollback consistency even when the served prompt text is clean.

Why it matters: Applications relying on agentic rollback or time-travel mechanisms remain vulnerable to prompt injection or state corruption unless the underlying KV-cache is explicitly restored alongside the text transcript.

entry.title: Towards Computational Provenance: Carrying Causal-State Evidence in Generated Text
entry.summary:
A controlled study demonstrates that neural models can embed detectable, verified causal-state evidence into subtle statistical patterns of generated text without altering the final output answer.

Why it matters: It provides a proof of concept for establishing computational provenance, enabling third parties to verify which internal neural pathways were executed to produce a model's output.

entry.title: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identify "rule blindness" in compliance detectors and activation probes, showing their verdicts rely on scenario surface features rather than governing rules, and propose the training-free Internal Compliance Score (ICS) for efficient auditing.

Why it matters: Deployed AI compliance guards may offer a false sense of security by triggering on scenario context rather than actual regulatory rule violations.
